title: Why Transformers Replaced RNNs — Train Many Positions Together
key_insight: During training, a transformer can compute representations for many positions in parallel. Attention then mixes information between those positions.
body:
## Train Many Positions Together

An RNN waits for the previous hidden state before processing the next token. The accelerator cannot do all time steps together.

During training, a transformer can compute representations for many positions in parallel. Attention then mixes information between those positions.

Because parallel processing loses the built-in notion of order, transformers add position information so “dog bites person” differs from “person bites dog.”
common_mistakes: Transformers read only the immediately previous token.
Parallel training means token order no longer matters.
Attention has zero memory cost at every sequence length.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Train Many Positions Together” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: This bridge explains the practical problems attention solves before Phase 6 teaches transformer mechanics.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Train Many Positions Together” situation, explain Why Transformers Replaced RNNs without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
